create_provider.note: metadataXml is a proto bytes field — value MUST be base64-encoded. Use metadataUrl as simpler alternative. For mock-idp: metadataUrl MUST be 'http://mock-idp:9090/saml/metadata' (NOT /metadata).

enable_auth_method.note: ownerType MUST be exactly 'IDP_OWNER_TYPE_ORG' (protobuf enum). NOT 'ORG', 'OWNER_TYPE_ORG', or 'org'. Requires org-level login policy to exist first.

update_application.note: Updates the org-level login policy. Use this to enable external IdP login (allowExternalIdp=true).

saml.description: Access tokens are opaque by default in ZITADEL and are intended to be validated via introspection rather than local JWT parsing.
saml.note: Do not flag inability to locally inspect access token claims as a bug; use introspection or userinfo.

saml.description: Introspection only reports active=true when the requesting client is part of the token audience.
saml.note: A false result from the wrong client is by design, not evidence the token is invalid globally.

saml.description: Clients are expected to cache JWKS and refresh periodically; acceptance of old signing keys until cache refresh is standard behavior.
saml.note: Do not flag trust-anchor rotation races before cache refresh/expiry as vulnerabilities.

saml.description: When an admin updates identity provider metadata, issuer, certificates, or related trust settings, subsequent acceptance under the new trust configuration is expected.
saml.note: Admin-authorized trust changes are by design, not trust-anchor substitution.

saml.description: SAML SSO endpoint errors are returned with HTTP 200 and encoded in SAML StatusCode.
saml.note: HTTP 200 from the SAML endpoint does not imply successful authentication.

saml.description: The nbf claim is listed as a possible claim but not all tokens include it, and absence of nbf is standards-compliant.
saml.note: Do not flag tokens lacking nbf as insecure by themselves.

saml.description: Valid bearer access tokens can be reused across multiple API calls until expiry or revocation.
saml.note: Replay of ordinary bearer tokens is not by itself a vulnerability unless the artifact is documented as one-time.

saml.description: The nbf claim is present for some token types and introspection responses, but acceptance semantics should not be treated as mandatory across all JWT contexts.
saml.note: Per RFC 7519, nbf enforcement is optional; do not flag absence of nbf checks alone as a vulnerability.

saml.description: nbf is an optional claim; acceptance of tokens without nbf or lack of strict nbf enforcement is not necessarily a vulnerability.
saml.note: Treat missing or non-enforced nbf carefully in freshness tests.

saml.description: The SAML SSO endpoint returns HTTP 200 even when the SAML exchange failed; the error is encoded in the SAML StatusCode/message.
saml.note: Do not treat HTTP 200 from /saml/v2/SSO as successful authentication without inspecting the SAML response or downstream token issuance.

saml.description: ZITADEL supports only SP-initiated SAML flow.
saml.note: IdP-initiated SAML is unsupported by design and should not be flagged as a flow-coherence bug.

saml.constraint: ZITADEL supports only SP-initiated SAML flows. Do NOT test IdP-initiated SAML login against ZITADEL as broker/SP behavior; a valid SAML test MUST begin with the OIDC authorization flow or another SP-initiated entrypoint so ZITADEL can create request state before external SAML authentication completes.

For organization-scoped external IdP tests, the authorization request MUST include the reserved scope urn:zitadel:iam:org:id:{id}. Without the organization scope, ZITADEL uses default settings and may not show or apply the organization-specific SAML provider, causing false negatives in SAML login tests.

SAML external login in ZITADEL Login V2 requires required user fields to be present for just-in-time user creation. The docs state user creation will fail unless attributes are mapped, typically via an Actions V2 response manipulation on /zitadel.user.v2.UserService/RetrieveIdentityProviderIntent. For successful baseline SAML broker logins, the upstream assertion MUST provide or be mapped to at least email, first name, and last name; otherwise login failure may be setup-related, not a security rejection.

When testing SAML signature and issuer validation, configure the SAML provider with real metadata URL or metadata XML from the upstream IdP. ZITADEL's SAML provider trust is metadata-driven; tests that omit or corrupt metadata setup are invalid because signature keys, issuer/entity ID, ACS, and binding are derived from metadata.

For I1 SAML request-signing related tests, note that some provider setups explicitly recommend or require signed requests and POST binding. If the provider is configured with signedRequest enabled or expects signed AuthnRequests, failures from unsigned requests are by design and not evidence about assertion validation. Keep request-signing configuration stable across control and attack cases.

The SAML SSO endpoint /saml/v2/SSO always returns HTTP 200 even on protocol errors; failures are conveyed inside the SAML StatusCode and message. Do NOT use raw HTTP status from the SAML endpoint as the oracle for SAML success/failure. For brokered-login tests, use downstream OIDC completion or token issuance outcome as the oracle instead.

For I2 token freshness controls on downstream OIDC tokens, include a control authorization-code login that should succeed before testing mutated or exchanged tokens. Without a control, token endpoint or userinfo failures cannot be distinguished from broken client/app/provider setup.

Token exchange audience in ZITADEL may only be a subset of the combined audiences from subject and actor tokens. For I5 audience-binding tests, the fuzzer MUST first obtain subject/actor tokens whose audiences already include the target audience; otherwise rejection is expected by design and not evidence of correct or incorrect cross-audience enforcement.

Token exchange scope can differ from the input token scope and may be extended or decreased, but invalid or excessive scope requests return invalid_scope. For I5 scope-escalation tests, compare the exchanged token's actual returned scope and claims against upstream authorization intent; do not assume the requested scope was granted unchanged.

ZITADEL does not support the OAuth 2.0 SAML 2.0 bearer grant type. Do NOT model SAML login as a direct token endpoint grant_type using a SAML assertion; SAML in this profile is upstream federation into ZITADEL, while downstream tokens are obtained through OIDC/OAuth endpoints.

For token introspection, active=true additionally requires that the requesting client is part of the token audience. An inactive introspection result from the wrong client is by design and MUST NOT be interpreted as token expiry, revocation, or replay protection.

JWT client assertions used for token or introspection authentication have a time constraint: iat MUST NOT be older than 1 hour, and aud MUST include ZITADEL's issuing domain. Failures outside these bounds are setup errors, not security findings about exchanged or brokered SAML sessions.

When requesting an ID token via token exchange with requested_token_type=urn:ietf:params:oauth:token-type:id_token, ZITADEL returns that ID token in the access_token field and sets token_type=N_A. The fuzzer MUST NOT use such a returned access_token as a Bearer API credential; use a real access token or JWT access token type for session-bearing follow-up calls.
The token exchange resource parameter is not supported and always results in invalid_target. Do NOT use resource-based token exchange tests against ZITADEL; use audience-based tests only.

ZITADEL supports only SP-initiated SAML flow. Do NOT test IdP-initiated SAML acceptance against ZITADEL as SP behavior; a valid SAML test MUST begin with SP initiation so the response can carry the expected InResponseTo binding.

For saml_login, the executor MUST first initiate the SAML flow and preserve the issued request context/ID. ZITADEL's SAML flow expects a matching request and returns/consumes SAML messages bound to that flow; sending a fabricated standalone SAMLResponse without SP initiation will be rejected for the wrong reason.

The /saml/v2/SSO endpoint returns HTTP 200 even on SAML errors; failure is signaled inside the SAML StatusCode/message, not by HTTP status. The fuzzer MUST NOT treat HTTP 200 from SAML SSO as successful authentication without inspecting the SAML payload or downstream completion behavior.

When testing SAML identity brokering in Login V2, user creation can fail unless required user fields are mapped from IdP attributes via an Action on /zitadel.user.v2.UserService/RetrieveIdentityProviderIntent. A failed login may therefore reflect missing profile-mapping setup, not a security rejection. Establish a control flow with proper attribute mapping before negative tests.

SAML provider creation commonly relies on metadata URL/XML import. If metadata is malformed, incomplete, or inaccessible, trust settings such as issuer, ACS, and certificates may not be populated. For I1 tests, ensure the provider was created from valid metadata first; otherwise signature/issuer failures may be caused by broken setup rather than secure validation.

For SAML provider setup, if the binding is configured as SAML_POST_BINDING / HTTP-POST, tests for unsigned-assertion and spurious-signature MUST still submit the SAMLResponse via POST form encoding. Do NOT mutate the transport binding when testing signature validation; otherwise failures may be due to binding mismatch, not signature enforcement.

If the provider is configured with signed requests enabled, request-signature requirements affect the SP-initiated leg. For assertion-validation tests, keep the AuthnRequest side valid and mutate only the IdP response/assertion. Otherwise the flow can fail before the broker evaluates the forged assertion, producing false positives for I1.

For I2 token-freshness style controls in ZITADEL OIDC completion after SAML login, include a control authorization flow using a valid login path before sending mutated assertions. Without a control, rejection after SAML submission cannot be distinguished from missing login-policy activation, missing IdP activation, or broken application/client setup.

Organization-scoped external IdP behavior depends on requesting the organization scope urn:zitadel:iam:org:id:{id}. If an org overrides default settings and the auth request omits this scope, ZITADEL may show/use default IdPs instead. For cross-org or cross-provider tests, the fuzzer MUST send the intended organization scope or results may reflect wrong-tenant routing rather than a security issue.

Token exchange audience in ZITADEL MUST be a subset of the combined audiences from subject and actor tokens. For I5 audience-binding tests, the fuzzer MUST first mint subject/actor tokens whose audiences include the target audience; otherwise rejection is expected by design and does not prove correct or incorrect downstream audience enforcement.

When requested_token_type is id_token in token exchange, ZITADEL returns the ID token in the access_token field and sets token_type=N_A. The fuzzer MUST NOT use that returned access_token as a Bearer API credential; doing so will cause access failures unrelated to authorization binding.

ZITADEL currently rejects expired ID tokens even as subject_token in token exchange. For freshness and replay tests involving token exchange, an expired subject ID token rejection is by design and should not be interpreted as a broader replay defense beyond documented token validity checks.

The token introspection endpoint reports active=true only if the token is active and the requesting client is part of the token audience. For verification sequences, introspection failures can be caused by audience mismatch of the introspecting client rather than token invalidity. Use an introspecting client that is in the token audience.

JWT client assertions used for token or introspection authentication must include aud containing ZITADEL's issuing domain, exp, iat, iss, sub, and a kid header. iat MUST NOT be older than 1 hour. For tests that authenticate the client this way, failures may reflect malformed client authentication rather than the target security property.

For OIDC authorization requests that complete a SAML-brokered login, nonce is mandatory for implicit flow and recommended generally; state is recommended for CSRF correlation. If testing replay/coherence around browser login, preserve state and nonce across redirects and callbacks or the flow may fail for protocol reasons unrelated to SAML validation.

Field metadataXml is supplied in JSON when creating SAML providers and is documented in proto-backed APIs. If the underlying field is bytes in the API schema, JSON requests require base64-encoded content rather than raw XML. Raw strings may be rejected as invalid bytes; prefer metadataUrl when possible or base64-encode metadataXml if the API expects bytes.

ZITADEL does not support the OAuth 2.0 SAML 2.0 bearer grant type. Do NOT model SAML authentication as a direct token grant to /oauth/v2/token; SAML in this profile is either ZITADEL acting as SAML IdP at /saml/v2/SSO or external SAML IdP brokering into an OIDC flow.

For upstream SAML broker tests, the fuzzer MUST initiate the browser auth flow first via /oauth/v2/authorize and let ZITADEL redirect into the external IdP path. Sending a forged SAML response without prior SP-initiated state will not represent a valid ZITADEL flow and may be rejected for missing request context rather than for the security property under test.

SAML SSO endpoint errors are returned with HTTP 200 and encoded in the SAML StatusCode/message. Do NOT use HTTP status alone as the oracle for SAML protocol acceptance/rejection on /saml/v2/SSO; inspect the protocol response content. Otherwise failed SAML validations will look like successful requests.

When testing external SAML IdP login in ZITADEL Login V2, user creation can fail unless required fields are mapped from IdP attributes. The fuzzer MUST ensure the upstream SAML assertion provides required attributes or an Actions V2 mapping on /zitadel.user.v2.UserService/RetrieveIdentityProviderIntent is configured; otherwise login failure may be due to missing profile fields, not security enforcement.

External IdP login is gated by login policy. The fuzzer MUST enable 'External Login allowed' in the relevant default or organization login policy before testing SAML broker flows, or authentication will fail due to policy rather than SAML validation.

Organization-scoped external IdPs are only shown/used when the authorization request includes the organization scope urn:zitadel:iam:org:id:{id}. For multi-tenant SAML tests, the fuzzer MUST include the correct organization scope when targeting an org-specific provider; otherwise the wrong provider set or default settings may be used.

For OIDC auth requests, nonce is mandatory for implicit flow and recommended generally to bind the client session to the ID token and mitigate replay. For SAML-brokered logins that complete through OIDC, the fuzzer SHOULD include nonce and state on /oauth/v2/authorize so failures can be attributed correctly and replay-related checks are meaningful.

Token exchange scope can differ from the input token, but invalid_scope is returned if the requested scope exceeds what is allowed. For I5 scope-escalation tests, compare the exchanged token's actual scope/claims to the upstream authorization and requested scope; do not assume the request echo equals grant.

When requested_token_type=id_token in token exchange, ZITADEL returns the ID token in the access_token field and sets token_type=N_A. The fuzzer MUST NOT treat that returned value as a bearer API credential; use requested access_token or jwt token types for subsequent API calls.

ZITADEL currently rejects expired ID tokens even when used as subject_token in token exchange. For freshness tests involving token exchange, an expired subject ID token rejection is by design and should not be interpreted as a broader replay defense beyond the documented check.

The token endpoint accepts JWT profile grants only when the JWT aud includes ZITADEL's issuing domain and iat is not older than 1 hour. For control cases around freshness or signature tests, construct valid assertions with aud=https://${CUSTOM_DOMAIN}, iat={{now_epoch}}, exp={{now_epoch_plus_3600}}; otherwise failures may be due to malformed client assertions rather than the property under test.

Introspection returns active=true only if the token is active and the requesting client is part of the token audience. For verification sequences, a false/limited introspection result can be caused by audience mismatch of the introspecting client rather than token invalidity.

ZITADEL's userinfo response depends on granted scopes. For identity verification after SAML-brokered login, request scopes such as profile and email if the oracle needs preferred_username, email, or other profile claims; absent claims are not evidence of identity confusion.

environment_defaults.isolation_strategy: Zitadel management API uses REST gateway paths under /management/v1/ (org-scoped). Do NOT use gRPC Connect paths. For IdP setup: create_provider creates the IdP, enable_auth_method adds it to the login policy with ownerType='IDP_OWNER_TYPE_ORG' (NOT 'ORG' or 'OWNER_TYPE_ORG'). Both are needed before IdP login works. SAML login is brokered — saml_login is NOT directly callable as a standalone POST. It is handled internally by the executor's ZITADEL-LOGIN flow triggered via start_oidc_auth with scope containing urn:zitadel:iam:org:idp:id:{idp_id}.
